title: AWS Introduces Strands Decider 2B and Strands Box for AI Agent Development
gist: AWS open-sourced Strands Decider 2B, a 2B-parameter decision model for routing, tool selection and guardrails, and Strands Box (developer preview), a kernel-isolated sandbox with a policy language for agent actions; benchmark results do not show an edge over TypeSafe AI's Jev.

insights.claim: Strands Decider 2B is a two-billion-parameter model that selects among predefined options with confidence scores rather than generating long text, for model routing, tool selection, classification, guardrails and context management.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Small decision models can replace large-LLM calls for control-flow, lowering agent cost and latency.
insights.locator: Strands Decider 2B is a two-billion-parameter model

insights.claim: It is based on Qwen3.5-2B with the language-model head replaced by a pointer head and a rank-16 LoRA adapter; AWS released weights, training data and scripts for local use.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: AWS is building on an Alibaba open model, an example of open-weight reuse.
insights.locator: The model is based on Qwen3.5-2B

insights.claim: AWS reports median decision latency of about 115 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 and 153 ms on an Apple M3 MacBook for small tasks, and 72.3% accuracy across 231 public JevBench tasks for the v19 checkpoint.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Edge-class hardware suffices for agent decisions; 72.3% accuracy is modest for production gating.
insights.locator: According to AWS, Strands Decider 2B achieved

insights.claim: It competes with TypeSafe AI's Jev: Decider is open source and local while Jev is a managed API, and the published JevBench results do not establish a direct performance advantage over Jev.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Specialised decision models are an emerging category; open vs managed is the differentiator.

insights.claim: Early feedback flagged GitHub issues with concurrent requests, Apple Silicon compatibility and cold-start latency, which developers should evaluate before production use.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez

insights.claim: Strands Box (developer preview) combines OS-level, kernel-enforced isolation with Dogwood, an open-source policy language, routing shell, Python, MCP tools, filesystem and network actions through one policy layer.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Agent execution control is becoming a distinct infrastructure layer.

insights.claim: Unlike container sandboxes and Firecracker microVMs that restrict filesystem, process and network access, Strands Box adds policies on tool arguments and prior actions, e.g. requiring tests to pass before pushing code or capping external API call frequency.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Stateful, history-aware policy is a differentiator versus conventional sandboxes.
insights.locator: Strands Box addresses problems also handled by

insights.claim: These controls operate outside the language model, reducing reliance on prompt instructions to enforce boundaries, and work with different models and agent frameworks locally or in the cloud.
insights.speaker: Daniel Dominguez
insights.so_what: Enforcement outside the model is the security design direction; low switching cost eases adoption.
